issues.description: The problem statement (UML and textual description) specifies acceptSupplyDelivery(String supplierName, String ingredientName, int price, int quantity) (four parameters), but the provided Main example and the solution implement/use acceptSupplyDelivery with three parameters (String name, int price, int quantity). This mismatch between the specification and the code will confuse students about the required method signature and prevent them from matching the expected API.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the acceptSupplyDelivery signature consistent across all artifacts. Either update the problem statement (UML and description) to specify the three-parameter signature used in the template/Main and solution (acceptSupplyDelivery(String ingredientName, int price, int quantity)), or modify the template and solution to implement the four-parameter signature (acceptSupplyDelivery(String supplierName, String ingredientName, int price, int quantity)) and update Main accordingly. Ensure the chosen signature is reflected in the UML, textual description, example Main, and the SealSaloon implementation.

issues.description: The problem statement specifies acceptSupplyDelivery should take four parameters (supplier name, ingredient name, price, quantity) and shows a UML signature acceptSupplyDelivery(String, String, int, int). The solution implementation defines acceptSupplyDelivery as static acceptSupplyDelivery(String name, int price, int quantity) — only three parameters and no supplierName. This mismatch in method signature (missing supplier parameter and different parameter ordering/names) creates confusion for students mapping the requirement to the implementation and for implementing the expected method signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the solution's method signature with the problem specification by implementing acceptSupplyDelivery(String supplierName, String ingredientName, int price, int quantity). Use ingredientName to update the stock and either record or ignore supplierName as appropriate. Alternatively, update the problem statement/UML to require three parameters (ingredientName, price, quantity) if the supplier name is intentionally unused.
